question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

claims.text: Merrill is the only firm of the five to explicitly name the mass-affluent client segment. Merrill (within Bank of America's Global Wealth & Investment Management) presents a 'Wealth Continuum' that names 'Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)' as a distinct client segment alongside 'High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)', and states it is 'Serving the wealth continuum of clients'. The comparison cannot include the other four firms on the same basis: Morgan Stanley names 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' and 'ultra-high net worth' clients rather than a mass-affluent segment (the only 'mass-affluent' mention is a third-party Cerulli Associates report figure, not Morgan Stanley's own segment); Schwab uses 'affluent' and wealth-tier labels ('high net worth', 'ultra-high net worth', households with $1 million to $5 million) but not the specific 'mass-affluent' name; Raymond James names 'high-net-worth' and 'ultra-high-net-worth' clients (its Private Wealth Advisor program defines high-net-worth as at least $5 million in investable assets), not mass-affluent; and Edward Jones has no passage naming a mass-affluent segment.
